extracted.intended_audience: general U.S. news readers interested in healthcare, business, and politics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating a company's public defense and actions during a pricing controversy (here: Mylan/EpiPen) including testimony in a congressional hearing and related access/price measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about price increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members requested documents and more information about the price increases; scrutiny focused on how the EpiPen two-pack rose from $93.66 to $608.61 since 2007.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full, timely documentation and clear explanations for pricing decisions (e.g., cost components, timing of increases). Avoid opaque or partial answers that prompt oversight requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access initiatives (discounts, direct-ship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mylan announced initiatives to make the auto-injector more accessible, including a discount card to cover up to $300 of the cost and a direct-ship option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement concrete programs (discount cards, direct-shipping, coupons) that materially lower out-of-pocket costs. Specify eligibility, limits (e.g., up to $300), rollout timeline, and how they will reach affected populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Launch lower-cost generic option promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: The company is working on creating a generic version that is expected to cost $300 and would be available for direct-ship and launch in the next few weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring lower-cost generics to market quickly when feasible; give clear launch timing and distribution details. Clarify whether the generic materially reduces consumer costs rather than preserving margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose profit margins and cost components to justify pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Bresch said repeatedly that Mylan makes $100 from each EpiPen pack after subtracting the costs of research, staffing and more; profit per pen was about $40 in 2015 compared to $50 now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable, itemized breakdowns of costs and profits when using them to justify price levels. Avoid vague or unverifiable claims about costs that fail to satisfy stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain executive compensation increases in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Bresch's salary rose from $2.45 million in 2007 to more than $18 million last year; she justified the raise by pointing to direct involvement in providing free EpiPens to schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect increases in executive pay to demonstrable corporate performance or public-benefit actions; be prepared to explain and document the link to stakeholders to avoid perceptions of unfair enrichment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer oversight questions clearly and directly
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked if the $300 generic price would go straight to Mylan and increase profits, Bresch was unable to answer clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise, direct answers for hearings and public questioning. Evasive or unclear responses undermine credibility; if unsure, commit to providing a clear follow-up with details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid business practices that exploit lack of competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Top Democrat Rep. Elijah Cummings accused the company of using a corrupt business model in repeatedly raising EpiPen prices, expressing concern about price increases for medication that lacks competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from repeated, steep price hikes on products with little competition. Consider market effects and public perception; adopt pricing that balances sustainability with fairness for patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with governmental investigations and contract probes
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of West Virginia launched an investigation into Mylan for possible anti-trust violations; the New York Attorney General's office launched a similar probe into the company's contracts with school districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively cooperate with state and federal investigations, provide requested contracts and records, and engage transparently with investigators to resolve concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate genuine social-responsibility efforts (e.g., free products to schools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bresch pointed to providing free EpiPens to over 66,000 schools in the past four years as part of Mylan's access efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measurable, verifiable public-benefit programs (donations to schools, access initiatives) to improve access. Ensure these efforts are substantial, well-documented, and not merely PR gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify who benefits financially from discounts or generics
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked whether the $300 generic price would go straight to Mylan and thus increase profits, Bresch could not answer clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether discount programs or lower-priced product introductions reduce consumer costs or primarily preserve company margins. Transparency about beneficiaries prevents skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and proactivity of remedy announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Mylan announced initiatives (discount card, direct-ship) after widespread public outrage at rising costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively address access and pricing concerns before public backlash; late or reactive measures reduce credibility. Provide clear timelines for remedial actions when announced.
